observation.visible_scene: A single dark, fibrous, partially charred lump (resembling a burnt piece of organic material with a hairy/tan interior surface) sits stationary on a scratched metallic tabletop. Throughout the excerpt, bright orange flames burn across and around the lump, licking its top, sides and base, while the lump's surface progressively blackens.
visible_changes: The flame shape and coverage fluctuate continuously frame to frame: at the start (t=0) a broad orange band sweeps diagonally across the middle and left of the lump; mid-segment (t=0.4–1.0) the flame wraps around the left flank and bottom and rises in tongues at the top-left; near the end (t=2.0–2.667) the flame thins into a low ribbon hugging the bottom edge and left side with only small tongues above.
The lump's surface darkens over time: tan/beige fibrous patches visible early become increasingly covered by black char, and the whole body looks more uniformly scorched by the final frames.

The right protrusion of the lump develops and maintains a blackened crust studded with small red glowing embers; this embered black tip is faint at t=0 and grows more pronounced and consistently blackened from about t=1.3 onward.

The lump itself does not translate across the surface; its position and orientation relative to the scratched background remain essentially fixed, so the apparent motion is from the flames and the charring, not object movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: What ignited the lump or what fuel/air source sustains the flame is not shown.
The identity of the material and the final outcome (whether it fully consumes or is extinguished) lie outside the excerpt.
Whether the flame intensity is overall decreasing or merely shifting is not determinable from the cropped window.
uncertain_details: Camera motion: the scratched metallic background appears stable across frames, suggesting a fixed camera, but no parallax reference confirms this.
Distinguishing true surface recession/ablation from mere darkening/occlusion by char and flame glare is not possible from these samples.
Whether the red dots on the right tip are embers of the same lump or reflections is inferred but not certain.
